The first release of Voxframe: turn a recording into a captioned video with
matching pictures, on your own computer.

## Downloads

| | file | notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows 10 / 11** | `Voxframe-0.1.0-Windows-setup.exe` | Not code-signed: Windows SmartScreen will ask you to confirm. [How to install](https://github.com/Ngum12/voxframe/blob/main/docs/install-windows.md) |
| **macOS (Apple Silicon) — early** | `Voxframe-0.1.0-macOS-arm64.dmg` | **Early build.** Unsigned, so macOS will ask you to confirm in System Settings. Apple Silicon Macs only. [How to open it](https://github.com/Ngum12/voxframe/blob/main/docs/install-mac.md) |

Check a download against `SHA256SUMS`, attached below.

Both downloads include FFmpeg 9.0.2, which is licensed under the GPL, as a
separate program. Its complete source is attached to this release
(`ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz`, with FFmpeg's signature `ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz.asc`), with
`ffmpeg-9.0.2-libraries.txt`: the libraries compiled into each build and where
their source is published. See
[THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES](https://github.com/Ngum12/voxframe/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES).

The first time Voxframe starts, it downloads its speech and picture models —
about 3.1 GB, or 750 MB for the Lite version — and shows its progress. After
that it works without the internet.

## What it does

- Captions every word as it is spoken, in English or French, and writes SRT and
  VTT subtitles.
- Matches each scene to a photo or clip by what is said — from your own library,
  or from free stock sources (Pexels, Pixabay, Openverse) if you turn that on and
  add a free key. Every image is credited.
- Slow camera movement, crossfades, title and chapter cards, and optional music
  lowered under the voice.
- A scene plan to change any decision — a picture, a caption, a card — and then
  update the video; only the scenes you changed are made again.

## Privacy

Your recordings and videos stay on your computer. See
[the privacy note](https://github.com/Ngum12/voxframe/blob/main/docs/privacy.md).
